_meta.title: UDL 3.0 + MTSS Alignment Map — Foundations of Constitutional Government
_meta.purpose: Machine-readable framework layer. Maps every recurring design element in the Government & Civics course to specific CAST UDL 3.0 considerations and MTSS tiers, with on-artifact evidence and a score. Invisible to teacher and student; queryable for district curriculum review and adoption defensibility.
_meta.udl_citation: CAST (2024). Universal Design for Learning Guidelines version 3.0. Lynnfield, MA: Author. https://udlguidelines.cast.org/
_meta.mtss_model: Tier 1 universal core (all students) · Tier 2 targeted supports · Tier 3 intensive supports, driven by progress-monitoring data.
_meta.scoring: present_strong = option designed into the artifact; present_weak = present but not yet operational course-wide; absent = single path only.
_meta.principle: The barrier is in the design of the environment, not the learner. Accommodations are designed in by default, not retrofitted. Firm goals (TN GC standards + SSPs), flexible means.

engagement.principle: Multiple Means of Engagement — the WHY of learning (affective networks).

evidence: Response choice on every task: write / say (record) / draw / build.
“Which Organizer, When” quick guide lets students/teachers choose the thinking tool.
Assessment response-choice: full form (A–D) or support form (A–B) as an access format, same standard.
Tennessee Connection on every unit ties national civics to students’ own state/community.
Verbatim primary sources and real political cartoons, not invented text.
Provocative real-world hooks open every standard.
Curiosity-driven hooks and ‘spot the bias / your verdict’ challenges.
GAP: limited game-like/playful mechanics in print; web edition is the venue to strengthen this.
Neutral-framing guardrail: no loaded language; ‘Who benefited / Who bore the cost’ instead of winners/losers.
Judgment is left to the student’s response line, never pre-decided in the design.
Verbatim ‘I can’ learning target on every standard.
Explicit success criteria (3-part) and cues per standard.
Scaffold + Extend columns on every organizer (Tier 2 support and enrichment on the same page).
DOK range 1–4 per standard; ‘choose your challenge’ CER levels at one firm standard.
Partner-first and ‘talk-first’ scaffolds; discuss options; card-sort collaborative moves in scaffolds.
‘Whose Voice Counted / Whose Participation Counts’ multiple-perspectives sections surface historically excluded voices.
Bilingual EN/ES presence signals belonging for multilingual learners.
Check-for-Understanding with answer rationale (the ‘why’), not just a key.
Progress self-check (‘how sure are you?’); teacher-side reteach; mastery analytics feed next steps.
Predict-first prompts (‘guess who this helped/hurt’) surface prior beliefs before reading.
GAP: could add explicit belief-check reflection more consistently.
Multiple-perspectives framing builds awareness of others’ viewpoints (SSP.03).
Historical-empathy prompts (SSP.05) ask students to view events as people of the time.
CER and ‘your verdict, because…’ reflection lines; progress checks; unit essential-question revisit slide.
Perspective-taking and ‘who was excluded’ framing build empathy.
GAP: restorative/discussion-norm structures are a teacher-guide opportunity.

representation.principle: Multiple Means of Representation — the WHAT of learning (recognition networks).

evidence: Print-first and digital; ≥9pt type, B&W-safe, WCAG-AA contrast; web edition scales/reflows.
Read-aloud-friendly text; primary sources presented as image + text; alt text on every image (bilingual).
Federalist and Anti-Federalist; enslaved & free Black Americans; women & the unenfranchised; the expanding franchise — named explicitly, not as a single ‘neutral’ narrative.
Frayer vocabulary; per-term definitions in plain language; key-term cues in organizers.
Phonetic pronunciation on every vocabulary term; sentence frames; word banks.
Bilingual EN/ES vocabulary and alt text on every term and image — designed in, not retrofitted.
Neutral-framing substitutions enforced in titles, band labels, prompts, and criteria (guardrail).
Text + verbatim source + image/cartoon + graphic organizer + slide deck for the same idea.
K-W-L reproducible; hooks activate prior knowledge; ‘predict first’ prompts.
Essential question per unit; concept webs and comparison matrices; cause-effect chains.
Primary vs. secondary source work; multiple perspectives; disciplinary practices (SSP.01–06).
CER and unit DBQ require transfer; cross-standard synthesis.
GAP: explicit cross-unit spiral/interleaving to be strengthened as units 3–7 build out.

action_expression.principle: Multiple Means of Action & Expression — the HOW of learning (strategic networks).

evidence: Write / say / draw / build response on every task; movement via card-sorts and gallery moves in scaffolds.
Digital format is screen-reader compatible; images carry alt text; print is high-contrast/B&W-safe.
Web edition designed for keyboard and AT access.
Students may express mastery in writing, speech (recorded), drawing, or a built product.
The full graphic-organizer toolkit; CER frames; DBQ; concept webs as construction tools.
Sentence starters and word banks → partner practice → independent performance; support-form items.
Response choice removes the single-mode penalty; reduced-choice (A–B) is labeled an access format at the same standard, not a lower expectation.
‘I can’ targets + success criteria make the goal explicit and student-facing.
Scaffold column anticipates common barriers; ‘Which Organizer, When’ plans tool choice for a task.
The graphic-organizer toolkit is a dedicated Strategy-Development instrument (Venn, matrix, CER, HIPPO, timeline, concept web, etc.).
Check-for-Understanding + progress self-check + mastery analytics (standard mastery, DOK weighting, remediation triggers).
Reduced-choice as access (never a lowered ceiling); bilingual by default; multiple perspectives; neutral framing — all designed to widen access, not track students down.

tier_1_universal.description: The platinum core instruction itself is Tier 1: UDL-embedded, all students, firm TN GC standard + SSP goals.
evidence: Every lesson is print + digital, bilingual, neutral-framed, with response choice and success criteria.
Primary-source-based inquiry with graphic-organizer support for all learners.

tier_2_targeted.description: Same standard, added support for learners who need it — designed into the page, not a separate worksheet.
evidence: Scaffold column: sentence frames, word banks, partner-first, card-sorts.
Support-form (A–B) assessment items keep the correct answer + one strong distractor.
Frayer vocabulary and pronunciation guides for language demand.

tier_3_intensive.description: Most-scaffolded pathway and teacher-directed reteach for learners needing intensive support.
evidence: Teacher-side reteach / priority-teaching guidance in the Teacher Guide.
Most-supported response mode (say/draw/build) available at the same standard.
1:1 conferring prompts and re-teach triggers surfaced by the mastery model.

progress_monitoring.description: The data layer that drives MTSS tier decisions.
evidence: Per-standard Check-for-Understanding with DOK tags.
Mastery analytics: standard-level mastery, DOK 3–4 weighting, remediation triggers, spiral interleaving.
Formative question banks with psychometric metadata for pre-field-test analysis.

design_contract: Every activity offers a firm goal (the TN GC standard + SSP) and at least two flexible means to reach it.
Every writable task offers response choice (write / say / draw / build).
Every vocabulary term carries a plain-language definition, pronunciation, and an EN/ES gloss.
Every image carries bilingual alt text; every page is print + digital, B&W-safe, WCAG-AA.
Every page carries a Scaffold (Tier 2) and an Extend option without lowering the standard’s ceiling.
Framing is neutral in titles, labels, prompts, and criteria; judgment is left to the student.
Multiple perspectives and historically excluded voices are named, not flattened into one ‘neutral’ narrative.
Reduced-choice and language supports are access formats at the same standard — never IEP modification labeled as UDL.

defensibility.IEP: Accommodations (extended response modes, read-aloud, reduced-choice access format, graphic-organizer support) are designed into the core materials by default, satisfying least-restrictive-environment expectations without a separate retrofit.
defensibility.504: Access features (high-contrast print, digital reflow, AT-compatible digital, pronunciation and language supports) are universal, not conditional on a plan.
defensibility.WIDA: Bilingual EN/ES vocabulary and alt text, sentence frames, word banks, and multimodal representation support multilingual learners across WIDA levels while holding the same content standard.
defensibility.GT: Extend options, DOK 3–4 tasks, honors prompts, and open inquiry raise the ceiling for gifted/talented learners within the same lesson.
defensibility.boundary: UDL never lowers the ceiling on a TN GC standard or drops an SSP. Anything that would change the skill assessed is IEP modification and is routed separately, not labeled UDL.
